source_excerpts.text:
# What the CrSBr population fit does and does not acquire

**Completed mathematical/source check, not an acquired physical layer model.**
The experiment demonstrates retained column-level Cr redistribution. Neither its
mean-population fit nor this check identifies a layer-specific move probability.
The SI maps intensity to populations by global min-max normalization; a
state-resolved intensity-to-count calibration is another required assumption,
particularly when hidden defect depths alter electron channelling.

Sources: [Nature article](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10431-9),
public SI PDF pp39–41, and the authors' [pinned notebooks](https://github.com/KleinAtomLab/Mesoscale-atomic-engineering/tree/6844cc568271d448704a0eb6ee55ddfd5246d242).
The main article body was not acquired. Local source hashes and executed checks
are in `POPULATION_RESULTS.json`; code is `population_interface.py`.

## Normalization and an explicit ambiguity

Write a=Gamma02 and b=Gamma20. For N independent three-state atoms with
native-to-each-interstitial rate a and reverse rate b, expected fractions satisfy
exactly the SI equations: p0'=b(p++p-)-2a p0 and p±'=a p0-b p±.
N cancels upon division of counts by N. Under this interpretation a,b already
are per-atom rates. The all-native column's first-event rate is 2Na, a different
observable. Dividing the fitted rate by N requires a different model/statistic.

Divide N=16 into independent blocks of size k, each moving together with
per-branch rate a and reverse rate b. Expected fractions obey the same equations
for every k in {1,2,4,8,16}, but first-change rate is 2Na/k. Code checks exact
rational generator identities in all 222 aggregate count states. For even k an
alternative block moves in equal +/- halves at total rate 2a and returns at b.
It also respects p±<=1/2 on every trajectory and has the same symmetric mean
law and first-change ambiguity; 19 states are checked separately. These are
identifiability countermodels, not proposed microscopic mechanisms.

At SI a=.992/s,b=.089/s, every model has expected native fraction .0580810 at
2s. No-first-change probability ranges from 2.676e-28 for independent atoms to
.0189112 for one synchronized block; native-fraction variance differs sixteenfold.
Resolved event sizes or correlations could distinguish these models. A mean
curve alone cannot. Deposited traces have not been cal

# Coherent control does not rescue this finite on-axis model

**Executed conditional model; new physical operation NOT_ACHIEVED.** This
extends the focus diagnostic to arbitrary complex superpositions of nine probes
and counts every Cr atom. It does not establish a measured displacement law.
Source: published CrSBr CIF from [the pinned author repository](https://github.com/KleinAtomLab/Mesoscale-atomic-engineering/tree/6844cc568271d448704a0eb6ee55ddfd5246d242).

Model: abTEM1.0.11,200keV,32mrad aperture,pristine6x4x16 periodic supercell,
256x256 grid,1Å slices. All768Cr atoms on32 distinct depth planes are counted;
the target column has16Cr. Incoming fields are sampled immediately before each
atom's containing slice. Each atom receives a periodic .4Å-radius disk mean
of |psi|². A common local-flux displacement coefficient is **unacquired**.
Other species, correlations, damaged-state feedback, phonons and inelastic
processes are omitted. Disk flux is not measured damage probability.

Focus values are -128,-96,...,128Å. For entrance modes psi_a define
G_ab=sum conj(psi_a)psi_b. M_j is target disk response; M sums all768Cr.
Coefficients c give incident power c*G c, target density c*M_j c, total
competing density c*M c. The largest generalized eigenvalue of (M_j,M)
optimizes target/total over this finite span. This is ordinary linear algebra.
Nonnegative time mixtures cannot beat the best ratio in the fixed independent
first-event model.

Built probes have squared array norm about1/65536. Assuming unit array norm
or pricing coefficient norm would misprice dose. Whitening with G charges
specimen-plane incident norm including interference; G condition number is
about1880. Probe preparation, aperture loss, coherence and control bandwidth
remain additional costs. Arbitrary coherent superpositions are an optimistic
enlargement, not a demonstrated hardware menu.

|Layer|Best single focus,target/allCr|Best coherent ratio|Target efficiency at best ratio|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|1|.15384|.32976|.21783|
|8|.15094|.15942|.46390|
|16|.17450|.32605|.24968|

Across16 layers, coherent maxima span .15691–.32976 versus .11531–.17450 for
individual focuses in the same library. Efficiency is target density relative
to its maximum at equal incident norm in the same coherent span. Maximizing
selectivity sacrifices about40–78% of that density. Saved support points for

# A retained, verified operation instead of direct-perfect writing

Failure of an illustrative99% first-event target does not exclude ordinary
heralding and retry. Suppose each attempt begins at the same verified native
state, proposes exactly one defect at the target with probability p, survives
perfect layer readout with probability q, and cleanly resets a rejected proposal
with probability r. All failed reads/resets terminate the run irreversibly.
These regenerative probabilities and one-defect/no-collateral contract are
unacquired assumptions, not conversions of fluence into physical fidelity.

Ordinary geometric-series reasoning gives

    S = qp / [1-q(1-p)r],    E attempts = 1/[1-q(1-p)r].

A goal S>=s requires r>=[1-qp/s]/[q(1-p)]. Even perfect reset needs
q>=s/[p+s(1-p)]. `heralded_interface.py`/`HERALDED_RESULTS.json` execute these
exact rational gates for explicitly declared illustrative inputs.

At p=.28,q=.995, even r=1 gives only .98237 eventual success. A .99 goal
needs q>=.997180 with perfect reset. At p=.68,q=.995, reset needs r>=.994239;
at q=.9999 the same proposal needs r>=.978848. False acceptance, write damage,
registry errors and unrecognized changes add costs. Repeated confirmation does
not suppress common calibration error as independent noise; extra dose counts.

The source's imaging-based erasure randomizes interstitial sites. Projected
reverse occupancy does not acquire a native layer reset. A conditional
counter-propagating lower-energy rollback candidate remains to be acquired,
including displacement thresholds, capture, other-species damage and flip/registry.
The missing operation is a joint proposal/read/rollback kernel on the same
specimen and envelope. Favorable component models do not establish that cycle.
An equally informed ordinary controller gets the same retry. No new principle,
physical no-go, or practical advantage is claimed.
